## Project Title

Analyzing Privacy Risks and Unintended Consequences in Data-Driven Recommendation Systems

## Project Description

The goal of this project is to examine how data-driven recommendation systems can create unintended privacy risks and downstream harm for individuals and groups. Using real-world examples and publicly available datasets, this project will explore how personal data is collected, processed, and ultimately used to influence user behavior.

This topic connects directly to current discussions around data privacy, algorithmic bias, and ethical machine learning practices, particularly in large-scale platforms that rely on user data.

## Research Question

How do recommendation systems contribute to unintended privacy violations, and what design or policy interventions could reduce downstream harm?

## Data Sources

This project will rely on a combination of:
- Publicly available datasets related to user behavior and recommendations
- Case studies from the New York Times Privacy Project
- Supplementary academic and industry sources on machine learning and recommender systems

No personally identifiable information will be used.

## Methods

The analysis will include:
- Exploratory data analysis using R
- Visualization of patterns related to recommendation behavior
- Conceptual analysis connecting observed patterns to privacy risks and unintended consequences

R will be used to clean, analyze, and visualize the data.

## Expected Outcomes

The expected outcome is a clearer understanding of how recommendation systems can unintentionally expose sensitive information or reinforce harmful patterns. The project will also propose high-level recommendations for improving privacy-aware system design.

## Ethical Considerations

Special attention will be paid to ethical issues such as:
- User consent
- Data transparency
- Algorithmic accountability
- Potential downstream harms

These considerations will be grounded in course readings and discussions.

## Conclusion

This project aims to bridge technical data analysis with ethical reflection, highlighting the importance of responsible data practices in modern machine learning systems.
